cases.description: The pivot_table argument points at an ordinary range, not a PivotTable
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If the pivot_table argument is not a range in which a PivotTable is found, GETPIVOTDATA returns #REF!." A1 is the top-left of a plain data range that happens to have a "Sales" header -- a deliberately tempting target, because an engine that treats GETPIVOTDATA as a glorified lookup would find the column and return 100 or 600 instead of erroring. HARNESS LIMITATION, stated rather than worked around: Microsoft's GETPIVOTDATA examples all read from a PivotTable, and a PivotTable is a workbook feature that openpyxl cannot author -- it can neither build a pivot cache nor lay out a pivot range -- so none of the page's four value-returning examples ($5,534 / $5,534 / $2,876 / $309) can be reproduced by this harness at all. What CAN be executed faithfully is the branch the page documents for exactly this situation, and it is the one that matters for a compatibility corpus: what an engine does when GETPIVOTDATA is pointed somewhere that is not a PivotTable. A3:B4 here holds a plain two-column range of ordinary values -- headers Region / Sales and three data rows -- which is emphatically NOT a PivotTable. Column F is untouched because this harness writes the formula under test into cell F1.

cases.description: The full field/item form, still pointed at an ordinary range
cases.expected_note: The same documented clause, exercised through the optional field1/item1 arguments that the page describes as "1 to 126 pairs of field names and item names".
